title: Ere to the World Again We Go
description: Ere to the World Again We Go in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 503, “Close of Worship”, where the book credits them to the Univ. Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Ere to the world a-gain we go, Its plea-sures, cares, and id-le show, Thy grace once more, O God, we crave, From fol-ly and from sin to save.

lines: Ere to the world again we go,
Its pleasures, cares, and idle show,
Thy grace once more, O God, we crave,
From folly and from sin to save.
May the great truths we here have heard —
The lessons of Thy holy word —
Dwell in our inmost bosoms deep,
And all our souls from error keep.
Oh! may the influence of this day
Long as our memory with us stay,
And as an angel guardian prove,
To guide us to our home above.

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1866.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
